reviewers.role: Prüferin (lizenzierte telc-B2-Prüferin): exam fidelity, rubric application, task clarity
Kursleiterin DaF/DaZ, Niveau B2.2: naturalness, level, didactics, scene plausibility

method: We read every German string again: start (Folge, gist, Auftakt), the LS1 AGB and its items, the LS2 dialogue, items, Aussprache and generators, the LS3 rule table, pool, reserve and cloze, the LS4 texts t1-t6, both blocks and the strategy cards, the LS5 speaking task (situation, cards, partnerData, aiRole, openingLine, hints, model turns), the LS6 writing task and model text, and check, proof, Porträt, Redemittel, story, Fokus, facts and extras. We solved all 101 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line, and compared each result with answer and accepted[]. We also traced the two generated LS2 dictations through src/components/course-v2/content.js (dictationItems) and src/lib/lesson/check.js. We checked hv3, sb1, m3 and sa against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/tb2.json and the rubrics tb2-m3 and tb2-sa. We checked the grammar ceiling against grammar-spine.json and rc.konditional-konnektoren (b2.2/rule-cards.json). We checked the lexicon against b2.2/lexicon.json and every lower level's lexicon (exact lemma, compound list_ref, Fugen-s and gloss comparison), and the load and sentence length against level-profiles.json (b2.2: newPerUnit 55-70, maxWords 30). We checked the can-dos against registries/cando/b2.json and curriculum/b2-2.md E4, the cast and story against casts/series.json and the b2-2.md E5 cliffhanger target, the dates and arithmetic by calculation, and the key positions of all choice items by script. Each of the 27 r1 findings was re-verified. Validator: node scripts/course-v2/validate.mjs content/course-v2/b2.2/units/u04.json returned FAIL. KEY-01 has 2 blockers. LEX-02 has 76 ratchet findings (down from 111): 55 are „recurs in 0 later units“, which cannot pass before u05-u12 exist, and 21 are receptive lemmas that occur once in the unit's inputs. LEX-04 has 1 advisory. 32 rules pass and 4 are skipped as level-scope. LEX-03, LEX-05 and LEX-07 now pass. node scripts/course-v2/check.mjs returned 0 errors on the unit and 0 on registries/lanes/tb2.json.
verdict: Much improved, but not exitable in round 2. 22 of the 27 r1 findings are fixed in the unit, and r1-F27 is accepted as an advisory. The Sprachbausteine and all other choice keys are now spread (3/4/3 and 9/11/9). Teil 3 is now a genuine plan-together task: the same card for both sides, all figures shared, open preferences and no hidden limit. The story now runs in one line: 200 € (LS2), then the written demand of 648 € (LS6, framed as before the call), then 450 € (t5), then 574 € (LS5). The lexicon validators LEX-03, LEX-05 and LEX-07 pass. The remaining blocker is KEY-01. The r1-F04 renumbering (mo1/mo2/mo3) moved the failure instead of removing it: KEY-01 treats the Auftakt as LS1, and BANK_KEY_RE has no slot for an Auftakt micro-output. No numbering can pass until the schema or the rule changes. Four MAJORs concern the unit's items and lexicon. (1) Letter and word cues still admit a known lemma: fehlerhaft (B1.1) in ls1-p05 and Gegenvorschlag (A2.1) in ls2-p02. (2) The new dictation sources dictate 30-34-word lines whose keys say „10 %“ and „14“ where the audio says „zehn Prozent“ and „vierzehn“. (3) The correction items do not say what to correct, so the dass and verb-first variants taught in this unit are rejected. (4) Three „new“ lemmas are variants of words already taught productively (Schadensersatz/Schadenersatz, Vertragsbedingung/-en, anderenfalls/andernfalls), which LEX-07 does not see. One MAJOR is a gate hole outside the unit: the r1-F01/F02 class rule (ITM-03 or a shuffle) still does not exist. There are 7 minors. Every open fix is small. A round 3 should close the unit-owned items in one pass, once the KEY-01 slot question is decided.

findings.owner: SCHEMA §2 BANK_KEY_RE + scripts/course-v2/rules/KEY-01.mjs (rule-smith), then the unit
findings.quote: KEY-01 x steps[0].microOutput.bankKey (b22-u04-mo2): micro-output key „b22-u04-mo2“ names LS2 but sits in LS1 · x steps[1].microOutput.bankKey (b22-u04-mo3): … names LS3 but sits in LS2
findings.problem: The r1-F04 renumbering moved the failure instead of removing it. KEY-01 maps the Auftakt micro-output to LS1 (walkMicroOutputs yields step null, so lsNr = 1), and BANK_KEY_RE allows only mo1-mo8. BLUEPRINT §3.2 puts the Auftakt into LS1 with its own 60-s micro-output. SCHEMA Start.auftakt requires a microOutput whenever an Auftakt exists, and TextStep requires one for LS1 as well. A B unit that follows the blueprint therefore has two LS1 micro-outputs, and no numbering can pass KEY-01: two mo1 keys collide, and any other number names the wrong slot. b2.2-u04 is the first B unit with an Auftakt (the u04 files of b1.1, b1.2 and b2.1 have none), which is why the conflict has not surfaced before. Nothing is misgraded today, because the three keys are unique, but the unit file fails validation.
findings.fix: Rule-smith and schema owner: give the Auftakt its own slot. Change BANK_KEY_RE to `(w|s|mo)([0-8])?`, make KEY-01 map start.auftakt to 0, add the row `b22-u04-mo0` = Auftakt micro-output to the SCHEMA §2 table, and let the evaluate-* functions accept it. Then key the unit as Auftakt b22-u04-mo0, LS1 b22-u04-mo1, LS2 b22-u04-mo2. Unit-only fallback if the rule is not changed: drop start.auftakt (as the other B u04 units do) and key LS1 mo1 and LS2 mo2. That loses the §3.2 Auftakt, so the rule change is preferred.
findings.proposedRule: KEY-01 fixture: a B unit with start.auftakt.microOutput and steps[0].microOutput passes with b22-u04-mo0/mo1 and fails with two mo1 keys. BANK_KEY_RE test covers mo0.

findings.quote: p05 „Die Möbelpacker haben nicht aufgepasst. Sie haben ___ gehandelt. (f…, 10 Buchstaben)“ → accepted [fahrlässig] · p02 „200 Euro sind zu wenig. Priya antwortet mit einem ___: 648 Euro. (Nomen mit gegen-)“ → accepted [Gegenangebot]

Gegenvorschlag (a2.1-u07, productive) is a masculine noun with gegen-, fits „mit einem ___“ and is the everyday synonym. Both answers are marked wrong. The r1-F12 letter count excluded falsch but not fehlerhaft.
findings.fix: p05: change the cue to „(fa…, 10 Buchstaben)“ or „(Nomen dazu: die Fahrlässigkeit)“. p02: accept Gegenvorschlag with acceptedWhy „Synonym: Gegenvorschlag = Gegenangebot“, or change the cue to „(gegen + Angebot)“.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-01: for a fill_blank item whose promptDe carries a letter cue (initial letters and/or „N Buchstaben“) or a word-formation cue („Nomen mit gegen-“), every lemma in the cumulative lexicon up to the unit that matches the cue, the blank's gender/case and POS must be in accepted or excluded by the German prompt. Fixture: ls1-p05 with b1.1 fehlerhaft fails.

findings.quote: l09 de „… eine Teilerstattung von 10 % des Preises …“ / say „… von zehn Prozent des Preises …“ (34 words, 4 sentences) · l13 de „… innerhalb von 14 Tagen …“ / say „… innerhalb von vierzehn Tagen …“ (30 words, 3 sentences) · content.js dictationItems: answer = accepted = [line.de]
findings.problem: The r1-F26 fix replaced l14 by l09 and l13. The generator takes the first `count` sources as whole lines and makes line.de the only accepted answer. The learner hears „zehn Prozent“ and „vierzehn Tagen“. A correct transcription with number words, or „10 Prozent“, is rejected, because check.js maps no number words to digits and does not strip „%“ (the same class as r1-F16). The lines are also four and three sentences long, typed on a phone with a single typo allowance for the whole line. The unit's other dictation (c06) has 9 words.
findings.fix: Change the source to [ls2-l03, ls2-l06]: „Das tut mir leid. Was genau ist denn beschädigt worden?“ (10 words) and „Ihre Mitarbeiter. Wir hatten das Verpacken bei Ihnen bestellt, das steht auch in unserem Auftrag.“ (15 words). Both are short and contain no numbers. If a numbered line has to stay, the generator must add the say form to accepted.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-07 (or ITM-10) over generators: a dictation.fromInput source line whose say differs from de fails unless the generated item accepts both. Advisory ITM/E rule: a dictation source over 20 words or over 2 sentences is flagged.

Other one-step corrections give correct German. „…, es sei denn, dass Sie den Schaden zu spät melden.“ is standard (es sei denn, dass + verb-final). „Haben Sie Fragen, rufen Sie uns an.“ and „Zahlt die Firma nicht, schreibe ich ihr.“ delete falls and produce the verb-first condition that this very unit teaches. All three are marked wrong. r1-F14 fixed the same pattern in c07 by accepting the variant, but the sibling items were not swept.

findings.problem: Three of the unit's new lemmas are words the learner already has productively, in a variant spelling or number: the Fugen-s variant, the plural lemma and the e-elision variant. LEX-07 compares exact lemma strings, so the r1-F07 class (review words sold as new) survives. Two of the three sit in the productive core, and Schadensersatz is the unit's title word. The SRS creates a second card for a known word, and the B1.2 spelling „Schadenersatz“ in a typed item is at best a TYPO. The gloss „damages, compensation“ is shared with Kompensation (this unit) and Entschädigung (B1.1), so a lex.glossTyped item on it (LS1 generator source) has no unique answer. De-allocating the three leaves 52 new entries, below level-profiles newPerUnit [55, 70].
findings.fix: Lexicon owner: make lx.schadensersatz and lx.vertragsbedingung promotions of, or variant notes on, lx.schadenersatz and lx.vertragsbedingungen („auch: Schadensersatz“ accepted in typed items). Handle anderenfalls as a variant of lx.andernfalls; the AGB § 4 and lp4 texts can stay. To stay at ≥ 55 new entries, allocate three receptive lemmas the unit already uses without allocation: Laderaum, Textform and lackieren (all three are glossed today). Give the compensation-type words distinct glosses (Schadensersatz „damages (legal claim)“, Kompensation „compensation (something in return)“). Mirror the result in spec.lexiconBlocks and specs.json.
findings.proposedRule: LEX-07 folds lemma variants before the cross-level comparison: identical compound list_ref, Fugen-s (Schaden(s)-), plural versus singular lemma of one noun, and e-elision (ander(e)nfalls). Fixture: b2.2 Schadensersatz against b1.2 Schadenersatz fails.
